name: Donald DiCostanzo
title: Initiative co-proponent, 2026 California Proposition 39; businessman (co-founder and former CEO, Pedego Electric Bikes)
background: DiCostanzo graduated from California State University, Fullerton in 1979 with a marketing degree from what is now the Mihaylo College of Business and Economics. He describes himself as self-employed since age nine and spent more than two decades in the automotive industry before entering the bicycle business, including, per one profile, serving as global president of Wynn Oil Company; this profile could not independently corroborate the Wynn Oil detail beyond that single source. (Sources: California State University, Fullerton, Mihaylo College of Business and Economics news story; Micromobility Industries speaker-bio page.)

In 2008, DiCostanzo co-founded Pedego Electric Bikes with his friend Terry Sherry, starting from a roughly 1,500-square-foot storefront in Irvine, California. As CEO, he built Pedego into what trade and business press describe as North America's largest electric-bike manufacturer and distributor, expanding to over 200-240 independently owned dealer stores across the U.S. and Canada and securing celebrity endorsers including William Shatner; the company is based in Fountain Valley, California. He was named to the Orange County Business Journal's "Most Influential People" list and its OC 500, was a 2017 Orange County Business Journal Innovator of the Year nominee, and won the 2021 Entrepreneur of the Year Pacific Southwest, Orange County award from Ernst & Young. (Sources: Pedego Electric Bikes press materials via Bicycle Retailer and Industry News; Orange County Business Journal OC 500 profile; Bicycle Retailer and Industry News, EY award announcement.)

Pedego sold a majority stake to a private-equity firm in 2021; DiCostanzo stepped down as CEO afterward but remained on the company's board of directors, and by the time of this profile's research was listed as Managing Partner at Experience Ventures. He is a board member of the Electric Bike Association and has spoken publicly on U.S. tariff policy's effect on bicycle manufacturing, saying he expects tariffs to push companies to explore more domestic and automated production. He is married to Roseann DiCostanzo and has two daughters, Deanna and Jessica. (Source: Micromobility Industries speaker-bio page; Orange County Business Journal OC 500 profile.)

DiCostanzo has no record of elected or appointed public office found in this research; his role in the measure covered by this profile is as a private citizen and businessman who is a named initiative proponent rather than a legislator. On July 16, 2025, DiCostanzo, Assemblymember Carl DeMaio, and State Sen. Tony Strickland filed the California Voter ID Initiative, later certified for the ballot as 2026 Proposition 39, with the California Attorney General's office; DiCostanzo is identified in campaign and legal filings as a representative of Californians for Voter ID, the measure's lead support committee. No public source found in this research states his personal reason for joining the initiative beyond his affiliation with that committee. (Sources: Reform California press release on the initiative filing; State of California Fair Political Practices Commission advice letter 25-119; content/measures/ca-prop-39-2026.json.)

DiCostanzo is also a named party, alongside Californians for Voter ID and Yes on 39, in Californians for Voter ID v. Weber, the campaign's unsuccessful lawsuit against California Secretary of State Shirley Weber's office over Attorney General Rob Bonta's rewritten ballot title for Proposition 39. News coverage of the ruling identifies the third petitioner only as "an Orange County voter" rather than by name, which is consistent with DiCostanzo's Orange County business base and with the case being cited elsewhere as involving him as a plaintiff in his capacity as a registered voter, though this profile could not locate a court document itself confirming his name on the caption. Sacramento Superior Court Judge Jennifer Rockwell denied the petition on August 6, 2026. (Sources: Metropolitan News-Enterprise, ballotlabels_081426.htm; content/measures/ca-prop-39-2026.json.)
